rationale: The claim strictly bounds rare-event simulation to estimating a conditional risk metric under a modeled base distribution, simulator, and hazard threshold, contrasting it with unconditional safety claims derived from test mileage. The primary source (O'Kelly et al., 2019) explicitly defines the evaluated risk as p_gamma := P0(f(X) <= gamma) under base traffic distribution P0 and simulator rollouts. Challenging conditions—such as distribution shift, unmodeled tails, or perception-rendering fidelity—reinforce rather than defeat the claim, as the claim itself and all artifact uses explicitly disclaim unconditional safety and unverified transfer.
limitations: Search was limited to the provided arXiv:1811.00145 preprint text and artifact uses.
Did not evaluate empirical numerical convergence rates or applicability to civil regulatory certification frameworks.
